data.name: Parikshit
data.long_meaning: Parikshit is the name of a legendary king in Hindu mythology, the son of King Janamejaya and Rishi Chitrasena. He is known for his wisdom, courage, and strong character. Parikshit's story is a significant part of the Mahabharata, where he is predicted to have a short but eventful life. He eventually becomes the lawful heir of the Kuru kingdom.

data.cultural_impact: Parikshit's name has been celebrated in Hindu folklore for centuries. He is remembered as a noble and righteous king, who ruled wisely and justly over his people. Parikshit is also known for his courage, particularly his encounter with the great sage Vyasa, who had taken the form of a serpent to curse Janamejaya. Despite the potential danger, Parikshit protected his father and the sacred Vedic fire, demonstrating his selflessness and bravery.
data.spiritual_significance: Parikshit's story holds deep spiritual significance for Hindus. Despite his short life, he is remembered for his deep wisdom and devotion to spiritual pursuits. Parikshit was a respected scholar, versed in the Vedas and the Puranas. The story of his encounter with Vyasa also emphasizes the importance of dharma and the protection of sacred fire. Parikshit's life serves as an inspiration for Hindus to live every moment to the fullest, no matter how short their time on earth may be.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Parikshit was the eldest son of Abhimanyu and the grandson of Arjuna in the Mahabharata. The name Parikshit carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
